segments.title: Kaiyo Maru reconstruction and wreck archaeology
segments.summary: At the Kaiyo Maru Memorial Museum, a reconstructed ship presents the archaeology of the wreck from which it was rebuilt.
segments.body: Kaiyo Maru is a reconstruction rather than an intact surviving museum ship. The original vessel was wrecked, and the reconstruction displays archaeological material associated with the wreck. Visitors can walk through the ship and examine the evidence used to present it. The museum is a compact example of maritime archaeology supporting the interpretation of a lost vessel. The deck was closed during this visit, apparently because wet weather made access unsafe.

evidence.note: The transcript identifies the vessel as a reconstructed wreck and says visitors can see the archaeology associated with it.
Dr. Clarke identifies the Kaiyo Maru Memorial Museum and describes it as the final planned ship visit of the trip.
